- The fiscal 2025 full year and fourth quarter on the continuing-operations perimeter are not supplied, so last-twelve-month EBITDA, total debt to EBITDA, net debt to EBITDA and cash interest cover cannot be calculated at 2026-06-30 or at any interim date; severity High; the action that would close it is the company's supplemental recast slides, and until then only the issuer's own adjusted leverage can be quoted, with its definition. - No result after the quarter ended 2026-06-30 is supplied, so every figure is dated at that quarter end and the fiscal 2026 year-end position is not established; severity Medium; the action is the fiscal 2026 earnings release and annual report. - The annual reports state no EBITDA and no adjusted EBITDA, so fiscal year EBITDA is calculated from statement lines with gross interest, and adjusted EBITDA for fiscal 2023 to 2025 is not supplied; severity Medium; the action is the issuer's fiscal year EBITDA reconciliations. - Cash paid for interest and for income taxes is not printed in the interim statements, so interim cash interest cover cannot be calculated; severity Medium; the action is the interim cash flow supplement. - No reported covenant ratio is printed and the credit agreement is not supplied, so covenant headroom is not calculable and is never inferred; severity Medium; the action is the executed credit agreement and compliance figures. - The legal rank, security and guarantees of the senior notes and the revolver are not stated by any source, so the debt stack and any secured or senior subtotal are not stated; severity Medium; the action is the executed indentures and credit agreement. - The balance sheet at 2025-06-30 is not in the sources, so the nine months 2025 column of the balance sheet and the interim comparison of debt are not stated; severity Low; the action is the third-quarter fiscal 2025 report. - Capital expenditures are printed as a total with no maintenance and growth split, so maintenance cash flow is not stated; severity Low; the action is the issuer's capital expenditure disclosure. - The revolver margin, floor and the exact maturity days of the senior notes are not stated in the sources; severity Low; the action is the credit agreement and indentures. - Statement cells printed as a dash are shown as not supplied rather than zero: impairment charges in fiscal 2023 and 2024, the defined benefit settlement loss in fiscal 2024 and 2025, net short-term debt in fiscal 2023, other investing items in the nine months of 2026, and impairment and held-for-sale losses in the nine months of 2025; severity Low; the action is the issuer's confirmation that they are nil. - Line items that a period statement does not present are shown as not supplied: proceeds from the sale of a business and loss on assets held for sale in the fiscal years, the component working-capital lines in the nine-month columns, and separate continuing-operations earnings in the fiscal year columns because the annual reports are not recast; severity Low; the action is the issuer's recast statements. - The amount of cash taxes on the Feminine Care gain paid by 2026-06-30 is not stated, so the post-period effect on net debt of the remaining tax is not separable; severity Medium; the action is the tax payment schedule.

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a payout-pressure reading is that payouts were 82.46% of three-year free cash flow, dividends stayed at USD 0.15 per share each quarter, nine-month 2026 buybacks were only USD 15.8 million, and the sale proceeds went to repay the revolver first. - Ownership percentages, holders above 5%, board committees, compensation and related-party transactions are not supplied because they sit in a proxy statement that is not in the sources, so the conclusion that no controlling holder exists is not fully established; severity Material; the action that would close it is the 2026 proxy statement. - The executed credit agreement, indentures and receivables agreements are not supplied, so restricted-payment, investment and priming capacity cannot be read and the legal-capacity link of every behaviour flag is not established; severity Material; the action is the executed documents. - Customer concentration is disclosed for one retailer at group level and one at segment level only, so the retained business's top-customer share is not established; severity Material; the action is the fiscal 2026 customer disclosure. - No continuing-operations mix is supplied for fiscal 2025, so the revenue mix shown for that year includes Feminine Care and cannot be joined to the nine-month 2026 mix; severity Minor; the action is the company's recast slides. - The July 1, 2026 impairment test result and any events after 2026-08-05 are not supplied, so impairment risk and later buyback or dividend activity are not established; severity Material; the action is the fiscal 2026 annual report and later filings. - The funding of the 2021 Billie acquisition is not described in the supplied sources, so acquisition appetite is not assessed from funding behaviour; severity Minor; the action is the fiscal 2022 annual report. - No credit rating or outlook is stated in the supplied sources, so the market view of creditworthiness is not established; severity Minor; the action is agency reports.

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence for a better view is that the retained business has stabilised: third-quarter organic net sales grew 1.1% with North America up 3.0%, Sun and Skin Care organic net sales grew 5.0%, interest expense fell to USD 16.7 million in the quarter, and management guides to adjusted EBITDA of USD 250 million to USD 260 million, which implies USD 72.3 million to USD 82.3 million in the fourth quarter against USD 78.9 million in the third. The view would turn favourable if fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA lands inside that range, Wet Shave profit stops falling and the 2028 notes are reduced or refinanced before 2028-03-02. facts.label: Revenue durability

spans.text: ## Request

This is the financial foundation for EDGEWELL PERSONAL CARE Co as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the audited annual statements for fiscal 2023 to 2025, the interim statements to 2026-06-30, debt at carrying value, liquidity, maturities and the company's non-GAAP measures, with the perimeter change from the Feminine Care sale kept visible.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Edgewell's net leverage worsened from 3.82x to 6.40x in FY2025 on lower EBITDA and higher net debt, then net debt fell USD 305.0 million after the Feminine Care sale, but no comparable current leverage exists, so creditors must lean on liquidity.
Basis: calculation C16; calculation C19; calculation C21; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6

Liquidity is the credit's strongest support: cash of USD 397.1 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 418.8 million at June 30, 2026 total USD 815.9 million, against USD 34.2 million of short-term bank debt and no bond maturity before fiscal 2028. The company's own adjusted net leverage of 3.7x rests on a definition that changed each quarter, and last-twelve-month continuing EBITDA is missing, so the leverage direction since the sale is not established.
Basis: calculation C23; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 43; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 11–12; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Leverage and cover

Reported EBITDA fell from USD 285.4 million in FY2024 to USD 185.6 million in FY2025, a fall of USD 99.8 million, because operating income fell from USD 199.3 million to USD 96.6 million after a USD 51.1 million goodwill impairment on the Feminine Care unit and USD 47.9 million of restructuring; with cash interest of USD 73.3 million the cash interest cover dropped from 4.54x to 2.53x, so a fixed interest burden now sits on a thinner earnings base.
Basis: calculation C45; calculation C17; calculation C20; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 89–91

The impairment is non-cash, which is the strongest argument against the weak reading: before it, FY2025 EBITDA would be USD 236.7 million and net leverage 5.02x, an Analyst Judgement shown beside the reported figures and not an issuer adjustment. What would make the weak reading win is the continuing earnings base, where reported EBITDA for nine months 2026 was USD 97.4 million against USD 158.0 million a year earlier.
Basis: calculation C43; calculation C44; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17
### Cash generation and shareholder returns

Free cash flow, taken as operating cash flow less capital expenditures on the consolidated cash flow statement, was USD 41.4 million in FY2025 against USD 119.5 million of share repurchases and dividends, so the revolver draw rose to USD 140.0 million at the year end; in nine months 2026 free cash flow was only USD 5.9 million against USD 37.3 million of returns, so shareholder returns, not internally generated cash, absorbed the balance sheet in FY2025, and in nine months 2026 the sale proceeds, not operating cash, drove the fall in net debt.
Basis: calculation C38; calculation C41; calculation C40; calculation C42; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 90–91; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 6
### Liquidity and debt maturities

Debt is USD 1,250.0 million of fixed-rate notes due in fiscal 2028 and fiscal 2029 plus USD 34.2 million of short-term bank borrowings, with the revolver undrawn at June 30, 2026; the earlier maturity of the revolver is the pressure point, because it is brought forward to 2028-03-02 if more than USD 150.0 million of the 2028 notes remain outstanding on that date, so the 2028 notes must be refinanced or reduced before then to keep the facility to 2029.
Basis: calculation C22; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 46; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 116–117
### Definition and data-quality risks

Adjusted EBITDA of USD 177.7 million for nine months 2026 is built from reported EBITDA of USD 97.4 million by adding back USD 80.3 million, mostly restructuring and related costs of USD 68.4 million, and it includes transition services income from Essity that lasts twelve months from closing, which was USD 7.7 million of the third quarter's USD 78.9 million adjusted EBITDA, so run-rate earnings are weaker than the adjusted figure alone suggests; the add-back realisation status is not stated by the issuer.
Basis: calculation C31; calculation C32; calculation C46; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13

Fiscal year columns are as first reported and include Feminine Care, interim columns are continuing operations, and the cash flow statements are consolidated in every column; ratios are therefore stated only at fiscal year ends, and the interim leverage and cover cells are marked not calculable rather than built across the two perimeters.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10
### Subsequent events and funding outside debt

The Feminine Care sale closed on 2026-02-02 with cash proceeds of USD 338.9 million and was used to repay the revolver; the company still expects about USD 55 million of cash taxes on the gain in fiscal 2026, the part unpaid at June 30 is not stated, and the third-quarter dividend of USD 0.15 per share was payable on 2026-10-08, with payment not confirmed in the sources. Receivables sold under the receivables facility and not on the balance sheet stood at USD 120.4 million at June 30, 2026, up USD 25.7 million from year end, and supplier finance obligations of USD 15.4 million sit inside accounts payable, so funding outside reported debt is rising and should be read beside the debt figures.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 18, 20, 43; calculation C47; EX99.1_2025-12-31_epc_ex991femdivestpressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1

## Gaps

- The fiscal 2025 full year and fourth quarter on the continuing-operations perimeter are not supplied, so last-twelve-month EBITDA, total debt to EBITDA, net debt to EBITDA and cash interest cover cannot be calculated at 2026-06-30 or at any interim date; severity High; the action that would close it is the company's supplemental recast slides, and until then only the issuer's own adjusted leverage can be quoted, with its definition.

- No result after the quarter ended 2026-06-30 is supplied, so every figure is dated at that quarter end and the fiscal 2026 year-end position is not established; severity Medium; the action is the fiscal 2026 earnings release and annual report.

- The annual reports state no EBITDA and no adjusted EBITDA, so fiscal year EBITDA is calculated from statement lines with gross interest, and adjusted EBITDA for fiscal 2023 to 2025 is not supplied; severity Medium; the action is the issuer's fiscal year EBITDA reconciliations.

- Cash paid for interest and for income taxes is not printed in the interim statements, so interim cash interest cover cannot be calculated; severity Medium; the action is the interim cash flow supplement.

## Findings
### Bottom line

No controlling sponsor is identified in Edgewell's filings, so creditor risk lies in payout policy: FY2025 buybacks and dividends outran free cash flow and were partly debt-funded, while the Feminine Care sale proceeds first repaid the revolver.
Basis: calculation C24; calculation C25; calculation C27; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 43, 46

The retained business is a two-segment personal care group with one retailer at about 17.4% of FY2025 net sales, a restructuring programme of about USD 92 million in fiscal 2026, and a Wet Shave unit whose fair value exceeded its carrying value by only 7% at the year end. Ownership percentages, board committees and the credit documents are not established from the supplied filings.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 78; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Key findings

- Governance looks like that of a widely held listed company rather than a sponsor-controlled one, which removes sponsor extraction as an evidenced risk but does not say who the largest holders are; share buybacks cut shares outstanding by 7.29% in two years.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 53; calculation C28

- Payout policy is the governance lever that matters: FY2025 buybacks and dividends of USD 119.5 million exceeded free cash flow of USD 41.4 million and revolver borrowings rose by USD 106.0 million, yet over three years payouts were 82.46% of free cash flow, so the pattern is pressure in one year rather than systematic leakage.
Basis: calculation C24; calculation C25; calculation C27; calculation C23

- The Feminine Care sale was used in a creditor-aligned way, because all revolver borrowings were repaid from the proceeds, but a new USD 100.0 million buyback authorisation still has USD 84.9 million unused, so a later switch of liquidity into buybacks remains possible.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44, 46; calculation C35

- The retained business is concentrated and under margin pressure: Wet Shave segment profit fell from USD 137.3 million to USD 106.0 million in nine months 2026 and the unit had only 7% valuation headroom at the year end, so a non-cash impairment is a live possibility.
Basis: calculation C18; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 78

- Seasonal working capital is the liquidity swing: first-quarter operating cash outflow was USD 125.9 million in fiscal 2026 and revolver borrowings reached USD 277.0 million before the sale proceeds repaid them, so the USD 425.0 million revolver is the seasonal funding source.
Basis: EX99.1_2025-12-31_epc_epcexhibit99112312025-htm.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2025-12-31_epc.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 43

- Finance leadership changed in 2024 and the chief operating officer left in 2025, but the audit opinion is unqualified and internal control over reporting is effective, so continuity risk is a monitoring point and not an adverse finding.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a payout-pressure reading is that payouts were 82.46% of three-year free cash flow, dividends stayed at USD 0.15 per share each quarter, nine-month 2026 buybacks were only USD 15.8 million, and the sale proceeds went to repay the revolver first. The view would turn more adverse if buybacks again exceed free cash flow after the revolver is redrawn, if a holder above 5% with control rights is disclosed, or if the credit agreement shows wide restricted-payment capacity; it would turn more favourable if the unused authorisation lapses and the retained business returns to organic growth, as it did in the third quarter with growth of 1.1%.
Basis: calculation C23; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 44; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so the conclusion that no controlling holder exists rests on the absence of a named sponsor and would change if a holder above 5% or any control right is disclosed.
- The credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so payout risk is judged from behaviour and not from restricted-payment capacity, which could be wider than past payouts show.

- Customer concentration is stated only for one retailer at group level and one at segment level, so the true top-customer share of the retained business is not established and could be higher than 17.4%.
- The fiscal 2025 revenue mix includes Feminine Care and no continuing-operations mix is supplied for that year, so the mix shift since the sale is shown for nine months 2026 only.
- Nothing after the third-quarter report of 2026-08-05 is supplied, so the July 1, 2026 impairment test and any later buyback activity are not established.

spans.text: ## Request

This analysis covers EDGEWELL PERSONAL CARE Co as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. It synthesises the company's fundamental credit profile from the nine supplied filings and releases and from the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance analyses. It gives no rating, security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or portfolio sizing.
## Sources

| EX99.1_2025-12-31_epc_ex991femdivestpressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl | Exhibit 99.1 press release on completion of the Feminine Care sale to Essity | 2026-02-02 | b106964af2ecca26ce0447c7350a71415de82147b6c3c0e58887e9949f9652d1 | Closing and price of the sale |

No source outside the nine files and the three supplied analyses was used.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Edgewell's liquidity of USD 815.9 million and the absence of bond maturities before fiscal 2028 protect creditors for now, but weaker earnings leave refinancing of the 2028 notes dependent on a recovery that the nine-month results do not yet show.
Basis: calculation C15; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 43, 46

Net debt was USD 1,187.1 million at 2025-09-30, or 6.40x reported EBITDA of USD 185.6 million, and USD 848.2 million pro forma for the sale proceeds received on 2026-02-02; pro forma net leverage is not established. Net debt was USD 882.1 million at 2026-06-30, but no earnings base for the retained business supports a current ratio, so the judgement rests on liquidity, a fixed-rate debt stack and management's outlook of adjusted EBITDA of USD 250 million to USD 260 million.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C06; calculation C07; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5
### Key findings

- Earnings, not debt, are the weak point: reported EBITDA fell USD 99.8 million in FY2025 and its margin fell from 14.11% in FY2023 to 8.35%, so net leverage rose from 3.82x to 6.40x (USD 848.2 million of pro forma net debt after the sale proceeds, with pro forma leverage not established) before the sale improved the balance sheet.
Basis: calculation C11; calculation C14; calculation C12; calculation C04; calculation C03; calculation C06; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Liquidity is the strongest support: cash of USD 397.1 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 418.8 million total USD 815.9 million, which is 1.09x the principal of the 2028 notes, so repaying those notes from liquidity would consume almost all of it and they must be refinanced rather than repaid.
Basis: calculation C15; calculation C16; calculation C74; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 43, 46

- The Feminine Care sale was a good use of an underperforming asset: it was 11.76% of FY2025 net sales but only 5.13% of segment profit and sold for 21.79x that profit, so net debt fell USD 305.0 million at little cost to earnings, although any shared costs it carried are not separated in the filings.
Basis: calculation C55; calculation C56; calculation C57; calculation C08; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 134; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 12

- Wet Shave is the largest segment and the main earnings risk: its segment profit fell USD 31.3 million, or 22.80%, in nine months 2026 and its margin fell from 15.31% to 11.80%, while the unit had only 7% of valuation headroom at the year end.
Basis: calculation C39; calculation C40; calculation C42; calculation C41; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 78

- Cash generation is thin relative to claims on it: FY2025 free cash flow of USD 41.4 million was 22.31% of reported EBITDA against 61.14% in FY2024, and returns to shareholders of USD 119.5 million exceeded it by USD 78.1 million, so the revolver rose by USD 106.0 million.
Basis: calculation C21; calculation C24; calculation C25; calculation C27; calculation C28; calculation C30; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 90–91

- Covenant reassurance is limited by definitions: the company reported compliance at 2026-06-30, but total debt was 7.61x reported EBITDA at 2025-09-30 against a 4.0x leverage test, so the covenant EBITDA must carry large add-backs and headroom is not calculable.
Basis: calculation C67; calculation C68; calculation C69; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 66, 116; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 43
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a better view is that the retained business has stabilised: third-quarter organic net sales grew 1.1% with North America up 3.0%, Sun and Skin Care organic net sales grew 5.0%, interest expense fell to USD 16.7 million in the quarter, and management guides to adjusted EBITDA of USD 250 million to USD 260 million, which implies USD 72.3 million to USD 82.3 million in the fourth quarter against USD 78.9 million in the third. The view would turn favourable if fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA lands inside that range, Wet Shave profit stops falling and the 2028 notes are reduced or refinanced before 2028-03-02. It would turn adverse if adjusted EBITDA falls below USD 250 million, if buybacks resume ahead of free cash flow, or if the next annual report shows covenant headroom narrower than the add-backs suggest.
Basis: calculation C58; calculation C59; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2–5, 14; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 64, 66
### Limitations

- Net leverage and interest cover for the retained business after the sale cannot be computed from the supplied statements, so the improvement from FY2025 is shown by net debt and liquidity and would be overturned if trailing earnings of the two continuing segments prove well below the outlook.

- No rating, bond price, peer leverage or sector spread is supplied, so the judgement that the business profile is average and refinancing capacity adequate rests on the maturity profile and liquidity and not on a market comparison, and a weak refinancing market for consumer credits would lower it.

- The fourth-quarter outlook is management's own and was issued on 2026-08-05, so the view that earnings recover in the last quarter of fiscal 2026 is untested and would change with the first results published after that date.

- Covenant definitions are described but not tested because compliance certificates are not supplied, so the conclusion that near-term default risk is low rests on reported compliance plus liquidity and would weaken if the definitions allow smaller add-backs than the figures imply.
- Fixed overhead that was shared with Feminine Care is not separated in any source, so the conclusion that the sale cost little earnings would weaken if stranded costs prove large.
### Strengths and weaknesses

- Liquidity and maturity profile is the first strength: USD 815.9 million of cash and undrawn revolver and fixed-rate notes of USD 1,250.0 million due in fiscal 2028 and fiscal 2029 mean no bond falls due before fiscal 2028, which gives time to recover earnings, although the revolver's maturity moves forward to 2028-03-02 if more than USD 150.0 million of the 2028 notes remain.
Basis: calculation C15; calculation C72; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 43, 46; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 64, 116

- Deleveraging by disposal is the second strength: the Feminine Care sale cut net debt by USD 305.0 million to USD 882.1 million at 2026-06-30 and repaid the revolver, which lowers interest expense (USD 16.7 million in the third quarter against USD 19.4 million a year earlier) and restores revolver capacity.
Basis: calculation C08; calculation C07; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 43; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3

- Brand breadth in Sun and Skin Care is the third strength: the segment grew organic net sales 5.0% in the third quarter, with strong Grooming and North America Sun Care, and earned a segment margin of 14.57% in nine months 2026 against 15.69% a year earlier, so one growing segment partly offsets Wet Shave pressure.
Basis: calculation C43; calculation C44; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 14

- Fixed-rate debt is the fourth strength: 97.34% of debt principal is fixed-rate notes, so interest of about USD 70 million in fiscal 2026 does not rise with market rates and only the 2028 refinancing exposes the company to new coupons.
Basis: calculation C73; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 46; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5

- Discretionary payouts are the fifth strength because they can be cut: dividends of USD 29.3 million a year and buybacks are choices, and buybacks were USD 15.8 million in nine months 2026 against USD 90.2 million in the same period of FY2025, which shows management can reduce them.
Basis: calculation C32; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 91; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 6

- Falling earnings are the first weakness: reported EBITDA margin fell from 14.11% to 8.35% in two years and nine-month adjusted EBITDA fell 9.66% to USD 177.7 million, so each percentage point of margin that is lost lifts leverage on a fixed debt stack.
Basis: calculation C14; calculation C12; calculation C37; calculation C38; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Wet Shave margin compression is the second weakness: gross margin fell 3.17 percentage points in nine months 2026 as inflation, tariffs, mix and plant consolidation outweighed productivity savings, and Wet Shave profit fell 22.80%.
Basis: calculation C48; calculation C40; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 5

- Leverage that is high before the sale is the third weakness: net debt was 6.40x reported EBITDA at 2025-09-30 (USD 848.2 million of net debt pro forma for the sale proceeds on 2026-02-02, with pro forma leverage not established), and the issuer's own adjusted ratio of 3.7x uses a definition that changed each quarter.
Basis: calculation C03; calculation C06; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Payouts above free cash flow in FY2025 are the fourth weakness: returns of USD 119.5 million against free cash flow of USD 41.4 million show that leverage was allowed to rise to fund buybacks, and USD 84.9 million of authorisation remains.

### Business model and credit linkage

Edgewell is a branded and private-label personal care manufacturer with two continuing segments, Wet Shave and Sun and Skin Care, sold mainly through mass merchants, food, drug and convenience retailers and online. Revenue is spread across razors and blades, sun care and grooming and skin care products rather than one product, which supports cash-flow visibility, but one retailer accounts for about 17.4% of net sales and orders are shipped within a month, so there is no contracted backlog to support debt service in a downturn.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 10–14

The business is seasonal: sun care sells from late winter to mid-summer, so the first quarter consumes cash (operating cash outflow of USD 125.9 million against USD 115.6 million a year earlier, consolidated) and the revolver was drawn to USD 277.0 million at 2025-12-31 before the sale. Cash plus revolver availability fell USD 139.4 million in that quarter to USD 365.8 million, before the sale proceeds, so the seasonal cycle can consume a large part of the USD 815.9 million shown at 2026-06-30.

Basis: calculation C18; calculation C19; calculation C17; calculation C20; calculation C77; calculation C15; EX99.1_2025-12-31_epc_epcexhibit99112312025-htm.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 14
### Ownership and financial policy

No sponsor or controlling holder is identified, so decisions on payouts and disposals rest with the board, and the record is mixed: shares outstanding fell 7.29% in two years through buybacks, FY2025 returns exceeded free cash flow, but the proceeds of the Feminine Care sale first repaid the revolver. Ownership percentages and the credit documents are not supplied, so legal capacity to make further payouts is not established.
Basis: calculation C75; calculation C27; calculation C21; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Revenue durability

Revenue is stable rather than growing: net sales were USD 2,251.6 million, USD 2,253.7 million and USD 2,223.5 million in FY2023 to FY2025, and organic net sales fell 1.3% in FY2025 on lower North America volumes in Wet Shave, Feminine Care and Sun Care. In fiscal 2026 so far organic growth was negative in the first two quarters (0.5% and 2.4% declines) and positive 1.1% in the third, so durability depends on the third-quarter recovery in North America holding and on Wet Shave supply constraints easing.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 58, 89; EX99.1_2025-12-31_epc_epcexhibit99112312025-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-03-31_epc_epcexhibit99103312026-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Margin resilience

Margins are the weakest dimension: FY2025 gross margin was 41.60% against 42.41%, adjusted gross margin fell 110 bp (20 bp excluding currency) as productivity savings of 270 bp were outweighed by 150 bp of core inflation including tariffs, 75 bp of mix, 45 bp of promotions and 20 bp of absorption, and in nine months 2026 gross margin fell 3.17 percentage points to 41.02%. Advertising and overhead rose at the same time (advertising and promotion 14.59% of third-quarter net sales against 13.56%), so operating leverage is working against the company while volumes are flat.

Basis: calculation C49; calculation C50; calculation C51; calculation C47; calculation C46; calculation C48; calculation C52; calculation C53; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 58; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3

Reported EBITDA of USD 97.4 million in nine months 2026 against USD 158.0 million a year earlier (a fall of USD 60.6 million) is on the continuing perimeter, and adjusted EBITDA of USD 177.7 million includes add-backs equal to 45.19% of itself and transition services income that lasts twelve months, which was 9.76% of third-quarter adjusted EBITDA. Run-rate earnings are therefore weaker than the adjusted figure alone suggests.
Basis: calculation C54; calculation C65; calculation C66; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 16–17
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital expenditures are moderate at USD 77.0 million in FY2025 (3.46% of net sales) and are guided to 3.0% to 3.5% of net sales in fiscal 2026, but cash conversion has weakened: free cash flow was USD 166.6 million, USD 174.5 million and USD 41.4 million in FY2023 to FY2025, or 52.46%, 61.14% and 22.31% of reported EBITDA, and nine-month 2026 free cash flow on a consolidated basis was USD 5.9 million. A split between maintenance and growth capital is not stated, so flexibility to cut capital spending cannot be sized.

Basis: calculation C36; calculation C23; calculation C22; calculation C21; calculation C26; calculation C25; calculation C24; calculation C31; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 91; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5

Restructuring and tax cash costs sit ahead of free cash flow: about USD 92 million of pre-tax restructuring charges are expected in fiscal 2026 with USD 71.9 million incurred in nine months (about USD 20.1 million to come), and about USD 55 million of cash taxes on the gain from the sale is expected in the same year. Management guides adjusted free cash flow of USD 80 million to USD 110 million, which excludes divestiture cash effects.
Basis: calculation C71; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 14; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 43
### Competitive forces

Rivalry is intense in Wet Shave, where The Procter & Gamble Company leads, BIC is expanding and Dorco competes in private label, and online and direct-to-consumer start-ups compete for shelf space; this explains the 7.2% fall in North America Wet Shave organic sales in FY2025 and caps pricing, so margin recovery depends on productivity rather than price. Substitutes and new entrants matter mainly through private label and direct brands, which is why lower private label sales from supply constraints in the third quarter hurt Wet Shave.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 60; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 4

Buyer power is the largest structural force: one retailer is about 17.4% of net sales and a few retailers account for a large share, so shelf-space or terms changes pass quickly into volume and margin. Supplier power is moderate because the principal inputs of steel, plastic resins, fabrics and chemicals are mostly available from several sources, but tariffs and inflation cost 160 bp of gross margin in the third quarter, which shows inputs still move earnings.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 14; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2
### Macro, regulatory and currency factors

Tariffs and trade policy matter to credit because they are in the margin: core inflation and net tariffs cost 160 bp of gross margin in the third quarter, USD 5.3 million of tariff refunds was received in the quarter after the court rulings, and no asset is recognised for further refunds, so any refund is an unbudgeted gain and not a base case. Sun Care is a regulated category and reformulation, recall and destruction costs of USD 3.4 million were incurred in nine months 2026, and the Middle East conflict disrupted international sales in the third quarter; currency was a small favourable factor in the third quarter, so it is not a primary driver.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 28–29, 46
### Credit-translated SWOT

- Strengths: liquidity of USD 815.9 million with an undrawn revolver, fixed-rate notes of USD 1,250.0 million with no maturity before fiscal 2028, and a brand portfolio with growth in Sun and Skin Care.
Basis: calculation C15; calculation C72; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 43, 46

- Weaknesses: reported EBITDA margin down to 8.35%, free cash flow of USD 41.4 million in FY2025 against payouts of USD 119.5 million, goodwill and intangibles above equity, and one retailer at about 17.4% of net sales.
Basis: calculation C12; calculation C21; calculation C27; calculation C64; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 14
- Opportunities: restructuring savings from the Wet Shave and Mexico consolidation, stronger fourth-quarter earnings that management expects, and possible tariff refunds that are not recognised.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 46

- Threats: a failed Wet Shave consolidation, retailer or private label share shifts, a refinancing market that is closed when the 2028 notes fall due, and an impairment that tightens covenant headroom.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 64, 78–79; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 4
### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale and market position are average: net sales of USD 2,223.5 million with a number two global wet shave position and a leading sun care brand pair give relevance but less scale than the leader in each category. Competitive advantage is average because brands are established but North America Wet Shave volumes fell. Business diversification is average: two segments and a split of U.S. and international sales of 54.15% and 45.85%, but one retailer at about 17.4%. Cost and capex flexibility is average: capital expenditures are 3.46% of net sales and shareholder payouts are discretionary, but restructuring cash costs are committed.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 14, 137; calculation C34; calculation C35; calculation C36; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Margin stability is weak, with the reported EBITDA margin falling from 14.11% to 8.35% in two years, and free cash flow stability is weak, with conversion falling to 22.31% of reported EBITDA. Ability to refinance is average: a USD 750.0 million note falls due in fiscal 2028 and the revolver can spring forward, but liquidity covers it 1.09x. Liquidity is strong at USD 815.9 million with no bond maturity before fiscal 2028. Financial policy and governance are average: no sponsor and clean reporting, but payouts exceeded free cash flow in FY2025 and a USD 84.9 million authorisation remains.
Basis: calculation C14; calculation C12; calculation C24; calculation C15; calculation C74; calculation C33; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

The trend since FY2025 is mixed: balance sheet strength improved with net debt of USD 882.1 million at 2026-06-30, but earnings weakened (adjusted EBITDA down USD 19.0 million in nine months), so the profile is better described as stabilising liquidity with unproven earnings than as improving credit quality. The main missing data are trailing continuing-operations EBITDA, covenant calculations and peer figures.
Basis: calculation C07; calculation C37; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are lower interest expense after the revolver repayment, restructuring savings and management's expected stronger fourth quarter, with an outlook for organic net sales of flat to 0.5% and adjusted EBITDA of USD 250 million to USD 260 million, which implies interest cover of 3.57x to 3.71x on outlook interest of about USD 70 million (an issuer-basis ratio, not a covenant test). The headwinds are Wet Shave margin pressure, tariffs, transition services income that ends twelve months after closing, and USD 20.1 million of restructuring cost still to come.
Basis: calculation C60; calculation C61; calculation C71; calculation C66; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5

Over three to five years the issue is refinancing: USD 750.0 million falls due in fiscal 2028 and USD 500.0 million in fiscal 2029, and the revolver matures in 2029 or earlier. The company can refinance from a position of lower net debt, but the terms will depend on whether EBITDA returns toward the FY2024 level of USD 285.4 million, which is not shown in the nine-month figures.
Basis: calculation C72; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 64; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Downside scenario

The initiating condition is a Wet Shave supply disruption that lasts longer than management expects: plant consolidation continues to constrain private label and international supply, a retailer reallocates shelf space to a competitor, and tariff costs remain. The first operational break is lost Wet Shave volume in North America, where organic sales already fell 7.2% in FY2025, with promotions rising to defend share. Financially, Wet Shave profit, which already fell USD 31.3 million in nine months, falls further and adjusted EBITDA lands below USD 250 million, so net leverage rises on an unchanged debt stack.
Basis: calculation C39; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 60; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 4–5

Liquidity absorbs the shock before leverage forces a decision: the first-quarter seasonal outflow, about USD 20.1 million of remaining restructuring costs and the cash taxes on the gain draw on cash, and a revolver that is used in the seasonal trough narrows the cushion for the 2028 notes. Management levers are to stop buybacks, cut capital expenditures and phase the remaining restructuring spend, and resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress before the 2028 notes fall due, on the liquidity shown at 2026-06-30, but a covenant test measured on a weaker EBITDA is the observable trigger because its headroom is not calculable. The primary downside path is a Wet Shave earnings decline that leaves the company refinancing the 2028 notes at higher leverage.
Basis: calculation C17; calculation C71; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 64, 66
### Overall credit view

Overall, Edgewell presents a not fully assessable business profile that is average on scale and diversification, supported by liquidity of USD 815.9 million and a fixed-rate debt stack with no maturity before fiscal 2028, but credit quality is constrained by a reported EBITDA margin of 8.35% in FY2025, Wet Shave margin compression and payouts that exceeded free cash flow. Cash-flow durability appears weak because free cash flow was 22.31% of reported EBITDA in FY2025, and refinancing capacity is likely to depend on Wet Shave earnings, liquidity at the seasonal trough and the springing maturity date of 2028-03-02. The primary downside path is Wet Shave earnings falling while the 2028 notes approach maturity. Further analysis would require trailing continuing-operations EBITDA, covenant calculations and peer data. Top risk: Wet Shave earnings decline before the 2028 refinancing.
Basis: calculation C15; calculation C12; calculation C24; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)

## Gaps

- Trailing continuing-operations EBITDA for the retained business is not supplied, so net leverage and interest cover after the sale cannot be calculated and the issuer's adjusted ratio of 3.7x cannot be tested; severity Material; the action is the company's recast supplemental slides.

- Covenant calculations and compliance certificates are not supplied, so headroom against the 4.0x and 3.0x tests is not calculable; severity Material; the action is the executed credit agreement and compliance certificates.

- Results after 2026-08-05, including the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 and the July 1, 2026 impairment tests, are not supplied, so the outlook range and the 7% Wet Shave headroom are untested; severity Material; the action is the fiscal 2026 earnings release and annual report.

- No credit rating, bond price, peer leverage or sector spread is supplied, so relative strength within leveraged personal care credit and market access for the 2028 notes are not established; severity Material; the action is agency reports and market data.
- A maintenance and growth split of capital expenditures is not stated, so capital spending flexibility cannot be sized; severity Minor; the action is the company's capital expenditure disclosure.
- Customer concentration for the two retained segments alone is not stated and the 17.4% retailer share includes Feminine Care; severity Minor; the action is fiscal 2026 customer disclosure.
- The legal rank, security and guarantees of the senior notes are not stated, so recovery and structural priority are not assessed; severity Minor; the action is the executed indentures.
